findings.summary: Code blocks appear before or without a stated one-line idea in places, and the 'Common Mistakes' bullets mix a problem with a fix in one line.
findings.evidence: "Function prop with no signature; write onSelect: (id: string) => void"
findings.fix: Split into two bullets: the mistake (function prop with no signature) and the fix (write onSelect: (id: string) => void).

findings.summary: The children table and the ComponentPropsWithoutRef bullets are mixed under one heading, and the 'Wrapper' bullet holds two ideas (the type to use and what it forwards).
findings.evidence: "Wrapper: ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'> (or extends it)" / "Forwards onClick, disabled and the rest via ...rest"
findings.fix: Add a short sub-label such as 'Wrapping native elements' before the Wrapper bullets, and state the idea in one line before the code.

findings.summary: Refs and Reducers combines two unrelated topics under one heading, and the @types/react bullet is a version note mixed into the ref bullets.
findings.evidence: "3. Refs and Reducers" / "@types/react 19: .current is writable; it was read-only in 18"
findings.fix: Split into 'Refs' and 'Reducers' sections, or add a visual separator, and keep the version note as its own labelled bullet.

findings.summary: Reducer code is shown with the `switch` on `a.type` but the state/action wiring (`s`, `a`) is not defined, so the snippet cannot be followed on its own.
findings.fix: Show the full reducer signature: function reducer(s: string[], a: Action): string[] { switch (a.type) { ... } }.

findings.summary: The 'Gotchas in .tsx' table has a row whose first cell is not a problem ('Or avoid it entirely'), so the table's Problem/Fix columns are misused and the row reads as a continuation of the previous one.
findings.evidence: "Or avoid it entirely | Use a function declaration"
findings.fix: Merge it into the first row's Fix cell: '<T,> or <T extends unknown>, or use a function declaration'.

findings.summary: Generic Hooks is described only as text and signatures with no code block, while the List component gets a full code block; the useFetch idea is a process that would read faster as a short snippet.
findings.evidence: "function useFetch<T>(url: string) returns { data: T | null }" / "Caller sets it: useFetch<User[]>('/api/users')"
findings.fix: Add a two-line tsx snippet showing the declaration and the call site.

findings.summary: The ‘Type Checking and Entry’ section mixes two unrelated ideas, and one bullet holds a command plus an unrelated claim about bare tsc.
findings.evidence: "Catch errors with tsc -b --noEmit or npm run build: bare tsc checks nothing in this template"
findings.fix: Split into separate bullets: how to catch errors, and why bare tsc checks nothing (the root tsconfig only references other configs). Put the Entry bullet in its own section.

findings.summary: The Create and Run section shows the command block before any statement of the idea, and the 'react-ts template' caption is a bare fragment.
findings.evidence: "bash npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react-ts ... react-ts template"
findings.fix: Lead with a one-line bullet such as 'Scaffold with the react-ts template, then install and run', and drop or expand the fragment caption.

findings.summary: The rules-of-hooks bullets and exhaustive-deps explanation are one flat list, and the exhaustive-deps bullet packs the rule, what it flags and where it applies into one long line.
findings.evidence: "exhaustive-deps flags reactive values used in useEffect, useCallback, useMemo but missing from deps"
findings.fix: Put exhaustive-deps under its own sub-heading and split its bullets: what it flags, and the two fixes.

findings.summary: The DevTools Profiler bullets mix several ideas (color meaning, the setting to enable, highlight updates) in a flat list with no grouping.
findings.evidence: "Colored bar = rendered; gray bar = did not render" / "Enable Record why each component rendered to see changed props, state or hooks"
findings.fix: Group under 'Profiler' and 'Components' sub-labels, or move the color legend into a small table.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet's Events and Generics section puts unrelated generic-component gotchas as flat bullets after the event table, so the page jumps topics.
findings.evidence: "Constraint: <T extends { id: string }> lets you use item.id" / "In .tsx a bare <T> parses as JSX: write <T,>" / "React.memo and forwardRef erase generics"
findings.fix: Add a separate 'Generics' sub-heading or small table (Need | Write) for the three generic bullets.

findings.summary: The Vite and Tooling section crams six unrelated facts into one flat list, and 'Lint:' and 'Profiler:' lines are unrelated to Vite.
findings.evidence: "Lint: rules-of-hooks (error) + exhaustive-deps (warn)" / "Profiler: enable Record why each component rendered"
findings.fix: Split into 'Vite' and 'Lint and DevTools' groups, or use a Need | Write table as in section 1.
